title: Integrated communication: Public discourse — the eulogy

frames.title: Lesson 110 · Integrated communication: Public discourse — the eulogy

body: **Foco:** Comunicação integrada: Discurso público.
**Pronúncia:** Ritmo e ênfase para nuances.
**24 palavras novas** (discurso público).
**Texto do dia:** conto e trecho de peça.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre elogios fúnebres a partir de uma cena de teatro, mantendo o ritmo e o tom solene.

body: Esta aula treina **ouvir e anotar informações (IELTS Listening, TOEFL Listening)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

frames.title: Reading · A scene from a play

blocks.title: Scene: The Eulogy
paras: (A small chapel. The mayor’s old friend, NORA, stands at the lectern. She unfolds a single page.)

NORA: We gather **not to praise** a title, but **to remember** a man. He **never** raised his voice. **Rarely** did he raise his own name. **Yet**, when the river flooded the lower town, **there he was**, carrying sandbags at dawn.
(She pauses, folds the page, and sets it down.)
NORA: I had prepared **a longer speech**. **Little did I know** how short the words would feel. **Let it be said**, then, simply: he **showed up**. And **that**, in the end, **is what we owe him**.
(Silence. A single cough. Then, softly, the congregation answers: “Amen.”)

items.q: Nora delivers a long, polished speech.
items.why: set it down; the words felt short.

items.q: The mayor raised his voice often.
The speech ends with a simple tribute.

head: Recurso
Exemplo
Efeito
rows: **Little did I know** how short words feel.
We gather **not to praise… but to remember**.
**Let it be said** that he showed up.

blocks.body: Advérbios negativos no início (*never, rarely, little*) exigem **inversão** (auxiliar + sujeito): *Rarely did he…*. Dão tom solene.
Sem inversão a frase fica errada: ✗ *Rarely he raised his voice.*

items.s: We gather not to praise a title, ___ to remember a man. (but)
Rarely ___ he raise his own name. (did)
Little ___ I know how short the words would feel. (did)
Let it ___ said that he showed up. (be)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.pt: As palavras de Nora foram tão simples.

items.ans: He showed up That was enough

body: **Pay tribute to** — prestar homenagem a
**Lay to rest** — sepultar
**Rest in peace** — descanse em paz
**Pass away** — falecer
**Show up** — aparecer
**Leave big shoes to fill** — deixar um vazio difícil de preencher
**Speak ill of the dead** — falar mal dos mortos
**Celebrate a life** — celebrar uma vida
**In loving memory** — em amorosa memória
**Be sorely missed** — fazer muita falta
**Nora’s words were so simple.** — As palavras de Nora foram tão simples.
**He showed up. That was enough.** — Ele comparecia. Isso bastou.
**Rarely have I heard a eulogy so short.** — Raramente ouvi um elogio fúnebre tão curto.

forms: Ela fez o elogio fúnebre da amiga.

blocks.title: After the service
lines: As palavras de Nora foram tão simples.

blocks.title: Pronúncia: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances

items.label: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances
items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

prompts.q: Begin with a negative adverb and inversion.
prompts.model: Never did he raise his voice.
We are here not to mourn but to remember.
Let it be said that he showed up.

blocks.task: Write a 5-sentence eulogy for a fictional neighbor, using two inversions and not to… but to….
blocks.model: We gather not to praise a title but to remember a neighbor. Never did he pass a stranger without a greeting. Rarely did he ask for thanks. Little did he know how many lives he touched. Let it be said that he showed up.

items.why: **graveside remarks** = palavras à beira do túmulo.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
